finding: Addendum to docs/evidence/syzygy-bpyt-6-3/dc3-fence-rules-2026-10-25.json (DC-3, the fence-rule finding). That record, its fence-probe-output.json and its mutant record are not edited; they describe the state before this change. This addendum records what the owner ruling of 2026-10-28 moved: the extractor, the index-link reader and the root-index reader now recognize fences by the PWB-REQ-006 profile, the link reader alone also its code spans, and G2 and G3 are fixed.

authority.whatTheOwnerChose: The extractor, the index-link reader and the root-index reader recognize fences by the PWB-REQ-006 profile; the link reader alone also recognizes the profile code spans; they use the profile recognizer, never its mask.
authority.whatTheOwnerDidNotChoose: C, and signal the stray span. Under plain C, two stray single backticks around a list of links make those links a span, and they drop with no signal.
authority.gateRule: GP-Q0: a change to what a gate accepts or refuses needs the owner; the mask, the policy action and scanActiveContent are unchanged (see differential.gate).

trackedProbeOutputIsStaleAgainstBase.note: The tracked probe output predates syzygy-bpyt.16 (the CRLF mask): re-run at the base commit it differs in the cases listed. It is left as it is; the before column below is the base re-run.

subject.note: The code commit holds every non-test source change; the test repair commit changes one test file only. Evidence commits after them change no code.

profile.change: recognizeCodeContexts exposes the fence ranges, the span ranges and the first malformation beside the mask; maskMarkdownCodeContexts is built from those ranges. The mask is byte-identical to the base on every text of the differential.
profile.recovery: The recognizer is total: an unclosed fence runs to the end of the text, a backtick opener whose info string holds a backtick still opens a fence, and a span still open at a fence opener or at the end of the text is dropped. The first malformation in scan order is reported. A caller handed a text with malformed set treats it as excluded (the gate does) and never acts on the ranges.

before.opener: three or more backticks or tildes at column 0, any text after
before.closer: the line, trailing whitespace trimmed, equals the opener run; or the line starts with the opener run and holds nothing else once backticks and tildes are removed
before.unclosedFence: everything after the opener is hidden; no malformed state
before.lineTerminator: CR before LF is removed first

after.opener: the profile: zero to three spaces, then three or more identical backticks or tildes
after.closer: the profile: zero to three spaces, the opener character repeated at least the opener length, then spaces only
after.unclosedFence: the recognizer runs the fence to the end of the text; a text the profile reads as malformed is excluded before this reader
after.lineModel: LF split with one trailing CR removed (unchanged); a line is fenced when the profile marks its first character fenced, so a text with bare CRs is a residual

before.opener: whitespace characters (a tab counts) up to three, then three or more backticks or tildes, any text after
before.closer: any later line that matches the opener shape with the same character and at least the opener length, whatever follows it
before.unclosedFence: everything after the opener is hidden; no malformed state
before.inlineCode: per line, each pair of single backticks with no backtick between them is removed (/`[^`]*`/g); a pair of double backticks removes nothing but itself

after.inlineCode: each character of a profile code span is deleted from its line, a CR or LF inside the span is kept, and a span may cross lines; the root-index pillar table reader keeps its code-span directory cells (it deletes none)
after.lineModel: LF split (unchanged); a line is fenced when the profile marks its first character fenced

G2.ruling: fixed: the extractor reads the profile fences

before.denominator: 7 of 25 well-formed fence-only LF cases differ from the profile

G2.pinnedBy: apps/three-surface-poc/src/fence-rules.test.ts, describe "G2, fixed: the extractor reads the profile's fences" (4 tests)

G3.ruling: fixed: the link reader reads the profile's fences and code spans

before.denominator: 4 of 25 fence-only cases, 3 of 4 span cases and 2 single-line span rows differ from the profile

after.denominator: 0 of 25 fence-only cases, 0 of 4 span cases and 0 single-line span rows

G3.pinnedBy: apps/three-surface-poc/src/fence-rules.test.ts, describe "G3, fixed: the link reader reads the profile's fences and spans" (6 tests)

extractorOnSpanCases.note: The extractor reads fences only, by the owner ruling, so the 4 span cases still differ for it (it never reads a span); this is not a gap.

gaps.G1_G4: unchanged (G1 was fixed by syzygy-bpyt.16; G4 is the consent reader, not moved)

probe.malformedNote: A case the profile reads as malformed never reaches a reader (the gate excludes it first), so its reader vector is the recognizer recovery, not an admitted reading.

gate.note: the mask and scanActiveContent are deep-equal at BASE and HEAD on every text: no text is newly refused and none newly accepted by the gate itself

residuals: Two stray single backticks around a list of links make those links a code span: they drop with no signal, and the text is well formed so the gate admits it. The owner chose plain C over "C, and signal the stray span". Pinned by a RESIDUAL test in fence-rules.test.ts.

The extractor and the link reader keep their LF-only line model. In a text with bare CRs (no LF) a fence that opens inside one reader line reaches the lines after it; the differential tallies base against head for those texts (diff.readerChanges, bareCrOrMixed) and makes no oracle claim for them. The bare-CR GAP rows stay.
The consent reader (outsideFences) and the Polaris renderer keep their own rules; G4 and the renderer departures stand.
A malformed text never reaches the readers; the recognizer recovery that makes it total is pinned by tests and is not a decision (the policy action is exclude-whole-artifact).
